controls.fault_model: Premature cleanup removes the old build immediately after staging its replacement, before handover.
controls.expected_behavioral_failure: The callback is reached, then boundary() cannot read or execute current/lamp-update because current still names the removed old build.
controls.limits: The candidate and fixed fallback still exist. This breaks the selected entrypoint, not every updater copy.

controls.fault_model: Non-atomic link replacement unlinks current before preparing the replacement link.
controls.expected_behavioral_failure: The occupied temporary link name makes replacement fail after pending is saved; current is now absent, so boundary() fails on the selected executable.
controls.limits: Old/new build directories and fallback remain. The guarded unlink lets initial install and ordinary successful replacements complete.

controls.fault_model: Handover points current at the staging name after staging has already been renamed to its final hash.
controls.expected_behavioral_failure: The post-link callback is reached with a dangling current; boundary() cannot read or execute the selected updater.
controls.limits: The final candidate, old build and fallback remain; this is a bad-target regression in the selected entrypoint.

controls.fault_model: Confirmation cleanup deletes the selected new executable instead of retaining it.
controls.expected_behavioral_failure: Confirmation returns Confirmed and clears pending, then boundary() cannot read or execute current/lamp-update.
controls.limits: The old build and fixed fallback still exist; the confirmed current entrypoint is broken.

controls.fault_model: Put-back deletes the failed candidate before the atomic restoration of the old link has succeeded.
controls.expected_behavioral_failure: The first put-back link blocker rejects restoration after deletion; boundary() cannot read or execute the still-selected new updater.
controls.limits: The old build and fixed fallback remain. The fixture later tests the distinct interruption after old is restored, before refusal is written.

controls.fault_model: The candidate is left under its temporary name although the recorded prefix says it was installed.
controls.expected_behavioral_failure: Old current runs, then build(NEW) fails because the final candidate path does not exist.
controls.limits: Does not break runnable current. It is not evidence for the runnable-current requirement or physical fsync durability.

controls.fault_model: The handover does not save its recovery record before attempting the link.
controls.expected_behavioral_failure: Old current remains runnable at the blocked link replacement, but pending() reports no handover record.
controls.limits: Does not by itself remove the current executable; proves the recovery record contract.

controls.fault_model: The post-link handover is announced without changing current.
controls.expected_behavioral_failure: The post-link boundary sees old bytes where the selected new bytes were required.
controls.limits: Old is still runnable. This is not a no-working-current control.

controls.fault_model: Confirmation reports success without clearing the pending record.
controls.expected_behavioral_failure: New still runs, but confirmed() rejects the retained pending record before it could allow a later rollback.
controls.limits: Does not break executability; proves final confirmation state.

controls.fault_model: Put-back clears its retry record before the new build refusal is durably written.
controls.expected_behavioral_failure: At the refusal blocker, old runs but the test finds pending missing rather than saved for the next retry.
controls.limits: Does not break the selected old executable; proves retry ordering after old restoration.

controls.fault_model: The ordinary updater handover no longer checks the explicit self-update opt-in.
controls.expected_behavioral_failure: The off-switch fixture expects parts-only Switched(2), but sees SelfSwitched and a selected new updater.
controls.limits: Does not imply an unexecutable updater; this is a separate opt-in contract.

controls.fault_model: An idempotence shortcut treats an already refused new build as a completed put-back, without clearing retained self.json.
controls.expected_behavioral_failure: The reconstructed post-refusal prefix returns Back::Nothing rather than completing Back::PutBack and removing pending; the earlier callback/blocker prefixes remain valid.
controls.limits: State-only: old current and fixed fallback remain runnable. This prefix is reconstructed from real back output and captured pending bytes, not an actual interruption at that line.

requirements_before_claiming_a_kill: Run the exact unmutated test successfully first.
Apply only one proposed production mutation in an isolated source copy; keep fixture bytes unchanged.
Require successful compilation and failure at the intended behavioral assertion; a compile error, timeout or unrelated fixture failure is not a kill.
Retain complete raw logs, command, exit status, source/test/patch hashes, and restore source in finally.
For R1-R5, confirm that the reached prefix lacks the selected current executable; do not describe a state-only failure as no runnable current.
limitations: Logical persisted-prefix recovery only: ordinary filesystems cannot reliably detect deletion of fsync calls by these tests.
Current-entrypoint failures do not mean every updater copy is absent: the unchanged fixed fallback is deliberately retained.
The scripts prove byte identity, mode and execution; they do not exercise real updater daemon exec, systemd restart or physical power cuts.
No control has been applied, compiled or executed by this preparation.
The post-refusal/pre-cleanup subcase restores captured pending bytes onto a completed real put-back; it is explicitly reconstructed, not a callback or blocker cut.
